newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest electricity eases in milder weather.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest electricity eases in milder weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. fell Thursday as milder weather was forecast through much of the area for Friday, industry sources said.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Friday peak, non-firm power prices were pegged lower at $17.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $30.00-33.00 on Wednesday for Thursday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
MAPP temperatures were expected to average four to eight degrees below normal through to Sunday, when warmer weather was expected at near-normal levels to Monday.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Friday were talked lower at $19.00-22.00 from $32.00-33.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
Temperatures in MAIN were expected to be near to 10 degrees above normal through Saturday then turning cooler with temperatures slightly below normal Sunday and Monday.
MAIN off peak next day power was said to be unchanged at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
In MAIN, Commonwealth Edison's 794 MW Dresden 3 nuclear power unit was in startup mode Thursday, returning from a maintenance shutdown which began Oct 26.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Friday were said to be discussed at $17.00-19.00 from $30.00-31.50 on Wednesday, the sources said.

Temperatures in ECAR were expected to be near to slightly above normal Friday, then milder through the weekend with temperatures five to 10 degrees above normal. Cooling was expected by Monday with temperatures returning to more normal levels.

In ECAR, Consumers Power Co continued to investigate the cause of a shutdown at its 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan and had not set a date for the plant to resume electricity production.
The plant was shut Jan 23 after a problem with electrical equipment at a main generator.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was assessed weaker at $22.35-22.80 from $22.80-23.00 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Friday delivery were pegged lower at $16.00-18.00 from $33.00-34.00 in the north and lower at $21.00-23.00 from $25.00-27.00 in the south of the region, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were assessed at $12.00-13.00 in the north from $17.00-19.00 on Wednesday while the south of the region was said to be again steady at $13.00-15.00.
March SPP was quoted at $20.25-20.75, while June SPP was quoted at $22.25-22.40 per MWh.
In SPP, temperatures were expected to average slightly above normal in the west and slightly below normal in the east Friday, then moderate to 10 to 20 degrees above normal by Sunday.
